questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That is was an english speaking country outside of Europe with interesting courses and a good city to live in

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was fine, not that easy but I figured it out

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got mails along the way, but talking to other exchange students helped a lot and there were also people to ask on campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just got it signed, was supposed to live on campus actually

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living in the city and getting familiar with another neighbourhood was pretty nice rather than spending all your time on campus. We also had an apartment-style dorm, which was SO preferred; it was better to live with two roommates and have a living room, kitchen, and two bathrooms rather than just a really expensive room near campus. Even though the apartments were a bit old.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were a guide that I followed how to register the right way as an exchange student, but would say it was confusing and nerve-wracking

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: a guided document

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful enough. I didn't get the courses that I at first thought I wanted. But I was content with the courses that I got. It was a bit of hassard and confusing with registering. The exchange register date is later than the official so many spots where already taken and I needed to get permission for institution leaders and professors to get in the classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to write to some different people at the uni to get in the classes that you want. That's sometimes the only way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was important to me that the courses weren't about something that I have had before, not first-year classes and that some of them aligned with the mandatory courses that I had to have merit for.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the style reminded me a lot of high school and even folkeskole way of teaching. Lots of small and bigger tests, group presentations and many many assignments. But I had less in class lectures but a lot of work sometimes out of class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
GIS for Natural Resource Management
Knowlegde, Ethics and Environment
Environmental Research Design
Enviromental Management 1

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
GIS for Natural Resource Management, was hard but beneficial
 
Knowlegde, Ethics and Environment, give new perspectives

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
rent was so expensive if you have an uni accommodation compared with normal apartments, rather find a nice apartment instead. I think exchange students or students that come far get a bit scammed with prices 

Coffe and some foods are cheaper than in copenhagen, which is soo good

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I was especially interested in the outdoor and ski clubs that do trips all the time
the wine society is also fun club, I was to one of their events
Many clubs give free stuff like mcgill merch, coffee and cake, stickers etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Rent a car and have some trips into nature or visit different cities. I did hikes and went to Toronto, Quebec etc. Clubs at uni also organizes trips as well. 
Explore the city you are in!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy, in Montreal you easily feel at home with the mix of Canadian and french culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes to things people do/the start of semester activities. At first, there are a lot of things happening, which calms down after a while, so go to it and meet other exchange students and students in general. Don't be afraid that you don't know people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That students in general were younger than me, which I could feel, but I got kinda used to it. In DK my age (23) is common on third year of uni but not in Montreal or other countries.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like the mix of Canadian and French culture. The people were so welcoming, sweet and open

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Join social activities (like exchange meet ups), especially in the start
- Join club events or sports team, I played volley and dodgeball 
- Remember that everything is not about school so go for trips, dinners, to bars... 
- Do not spend too much time missing home, calling your friends/family every day. That will just make you miss home more and not enjoy fully where you are

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't take all your courses at Macdonald campus, if you're interested in courses there, go two times a week, but not every day. It can take between 35-55 min to go one way with the bus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Connecting with other exchange students and living somewhere totally new and different for a long period

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on my own for 4,5 months, away from family and friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
